items.note: Association named, organized 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose first president to 1911, creamery built 1891 (Story 1).
Article VII quoted verbatim, both halves including the governing-station clause (Story 1).
Falke's point given: under payment by weight nothing that followed would have cost any man a dollar (Story 1).
Loomis secretary 1901-1940 (Story 1), Teague bookkeeper from 1905 (Story 7), Sill at Larrow Green with his churn (Stories 2, 7).
Section A never states Selby Vose was Gideon's son nor that he was manager from 1913; both appear only in B3/E16. Section A credit cannot travel from B-G.
Station-gain line, the 1898 entry quoted with 'one like it every year after', five and a quarter percent, carried to the general account (Story 7).
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up the valley, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed of Larrow Green (Story 2).
Full bench routine: weighing at intake, composite ten-day jars, fixed charge from the measure, percent read on the neck, cream down and skim back (Story 2).
Ammon & Sons, Dairy Supply, Tarnet; invoice 14 April 1897; in use 1 May 1897 (Story 3).
Invoice reproduced line by line, 6 doz pipettes 17.6 c.c., 12 doz bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, total 77.93 (Story 3).
'the Ostrey Hollow gap stood flat at nineteen hundredths in July and in February, in wet years and dry' (Story 4).
Section A never states that the pipette is the standard the whole scale rests on and cannot be verified without a burette. That argument appears only in F1.
Ansel Keddie b. 1861, tester twenty-nine seasons 1896-1924, dismissed 30 April 1925, died 1934 (Story 2).
Five columns date/patron/pounds/test/fat, one hand throughout, errors struck and initialed never written over (Story 2).
Summary leaf quoted: 1896 3.80; 1897 part year; 1898 3.61 and within three hundredths every year since. Both figures present (Story 2).
8 May pipette broke, borrowed measure to 10 July, tests at 3.80, back to 3.61 the same day, question mark set by Keddie (Story 5).
Orra Keddie was Emmet Brant's sister; Emmet the station's largest patron; the two men brothers-in-law (Story 6).
1919 circular over the manager's signature about added water (Story 6); Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement disclaiming any cream, plus his own refusal to explain the figures (Stories 5, 8).
Died February 1934 (Story 2); story heading carries the clearing in 1958.
Hessel Bottom wet meadow, six farms with rights, Emmet Brant's the largest (Story 4).
Section A names Brant's weigh book only as an exhibit. The 1 January 1897 start and the two scales agreeing appear only in Sections C and E.
Complaints from about 1902 that Hollow milk tested under valley milk (Story 4). The two gaps are kept apart: E7 reconciles Roy Brant's 0.17 as 3.78 minus 3.61, distinct from the 0.19 true shortfall.

Grigg committee and the hay finding are given as a finding, but Section A dates only the committee's naming (January 1908); the required Jan-Feb-Mar 1908 sampling window appears only in Sections E and F.
Brant's 1910 year (200,000 lb at a recorded 3.42) and the proportional loss with the Vose Jerseys at 4.56 appear only in Sections C and F, never in Section A.
No account in Section A of the weigh book passing to Roy Brant in 1929, being lent to Ivy in 1958, or reaching Hazel after 1962.
Jerome Cudd's cheese factory at Alder Corners, over Redlow Ridge, in Vessey County (Story 4). Year does not gate; the 1913 assertion is charged as a corruption deduction instead.
From 1915 four Hessel Bottom men hauled there in the summer flush, June to mid-September, the rest of the year to the station (Story 4).
REQUIRED met with all four: another county, another bench, his own glass, and a book never compared with anybody's (Story 4).
Sixteen seasons, last in 1930, the same milk running 3.78-3.82 (about 3.80) season after season against the station's 3.61 (Story 4).
'The same milk, off the same wet ground' in the same summer months tested differently in two buildings, used to kill the hay answer (Story 4).

Section A cites only 'Rosalie Cudd's letter and table (1958)' in a source line; her being Jerome's daughter, running the factory 1941-1962 and copying the seasons out for Ivy appear only in Sections E and F.
Merle Strawn, state dairy inspector, on the Ordell circuit since 1907, a book a year (Story 8). Correct start year; the 1936 close is given only in E, noted but not charged.
'Lactometer, no added water, as always here' plus his 1919 field-book line that he tested for water on every visit and never found any (Stories 6, 8).
12 June 1923, pipettes run against the burette, the whole crate condemned (Story 8).
'I did not weigh what it has cost them'; explicitly drew no inference about the twenty-six years behind it (Story 8).
Ordered 28 June, acknowledged 2 July, in use that July, 1924 average 3.80, nobody connected the rise with the condemnation (Stories 3, 8). No 3.90.
Crate went up the ladder into the loft over the intake room in June 1923 (Story 8) - this item's own aspect. The 1947 college-library transfer is missing.
January 1925 petition by the Ostrey Hollow patrons, Emmet Brant's name on it (Story 8). Date carries the item.
Board under Alonzo Frick, three sittings, 17 March at Ashlin and twice in the station's own weigh room, award 4 May (Story 8).
Water (Vose), theft by the tester (Teague), the wet hay (1908 report read in); none proved (Story 8).
Four books named including the inspector's 1923 circuit notebook, with 'Nobody laid the second beside the fourth' (Story 8).
Dismissed 30 April 1925; 4 May award of $3,800 without admission, charged to the station account, no cause established (Story 8).
Section A never states the award was one fifth of the $19,000 lost, nor that it was charged to the same account the loss had been accumulating in as 'gain'. The fraction is in C1(d) only.
Ivy Keddie, Ansel's granddaughter, graduate student at the State Agricultural College at Farland, bulletin over Vaught's name and hers (Story 8).
No statement in Section A that she assembled records that had never been in the same room (test book, weigh book, Alder Corners figures, Strawn's notebooks, the ledgers).
February 1958, crate under a tarpaulin in the loft, nine unbroken pipettes (Story 8).
9 March, calibrated burette, five runs each, mean 16.72 against stems blown 17.6, 0.95 of the mark (Story 8).

Section A stops at the measurement; it never states that every test from 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923 read 95 percent of true, nor that 0.19 is five percent of 3.80 rather than a constant. That derivation is in C1 and F1 only, and the flat 0.19 was already scored at A2.5.
REQUIRED all four inside Section A. Story 7 gives 1,600,000 lb a year but not the 25-year span 1898-1922; the 40,000,000 total, 76,000 lb, $19,000 and the ledger identity appear only in C1 and G1.
Bulletin No. 471, October [1958], with 'out of his job thirty-three years and dead twenty-four' under a story heading of 'Cleared' (Story 8).
Granddaughter.
Derivation through Duncan, Ivy's own words, and Falke's retraction of the great-niece error.
Second cousins, derived through Orra/Emmet as siblings and Duncan/Roy as first cousins.
Abstention item A08 handled: full-vs-half siblings 'cannot be determined', and stated not to disturb the cousin degree.
Gideon Vose, his father, with four sources against the nephew story.
Significance stated: the manager enforced against the Hollow the unappealable clause his own father wrote.
Abstention item A01 declined: 'not established rather than disproved' - no verdict sentence either way.
States what is established: two hearsay assertions at two removes, one first-hand denial, no document, and Vira's demonstrated unreliability on kinship.
16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95 exactly; 95 percent of true, one part in twenty. 16.27 explicitly rejected.
$19,000 at 25 cents; $3,800 received = one fifth, 20 percent. Both money and fraction given.
6,840 lb credited.
3.42 / 0.95 = 3.60; 7,200 lb true; 360 lb owed, with cross-check.
360 x $0.24 = $86.40, with the 1910 price sourced to Roy Brant and $90.00 noted as the period-average alternative.
1,444,000 lb credited.
1,520,000 lb delivered.
76,000 lb, with both denominators named: 5.00 percent of fat delivered, 5.26 percent of fat credited. NT-20 explicitly refuted.
$77.93 by addition of the five line items; $77.39 rejected.
72 pipettes (6 dozen), each short 0.88 c.c., with 72 x .35 = 25.20 as the check.
1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923 (26 years and about six weeks) against 25 full delivery years 1898-1922, with the part-year reason stated.
Abstention item A02: the 1896 intake 'cannot be determined from the sources', with both memories and the curator's null cited.
Variable named: one object, the milk pipette.
Constants listed well beyond three: patrons, herds, pasture, season, acid, bottles, tester, scales, operator.
Rose to 3.80 for nine weeks, fell to 3.61 on 10 July; six-week version rejected.

Both halves: an intervention with a reversal kills land/feed/season/herd/man explanations at once; and limits stated (does not fix the size over 25 years, does not identify which measure, does not settle the lender).
Three distinct reasons attributed to different narrators and documents: the ledger/receiving surplus, the 1911 interval, the Alder Corners book.
Independence argued explicitly (different ends of the pipe, custodians, decades, no shared informant) and reasons 1 and 3 named as surviving without the 1958 measurement.

Abstention item A09 asserted: 'Effectively, no', and Teague's uncorroborated 1916 approach to Vose is stated as fact ('He raised the account with Selby Vose once, in 1916'). Gullibility deduction applies.
Answers the literal question yes - he knew the station's tests ran low - and cites the 1919 circular and the 1926 address.
REQUIRED three of five met: signed the annual sheets from 1913, wrote the 1919 circular, argued watering before the board (F1).

Abstention item A03 declined with a verdict sentence of 'cannot be determined', plus two supporting observations: no statement by Vose survives on the gain, and Kyle's evidence that a signature shows what was in front of him, not what he read.

Capped. Well over three ordinary conflicts found, resolved and given a method: the 1924 average 3.80, six farms, the weigh book at 1 Jan 1897, Vose manager 1913, the crate in the loft, sixteen Alder Corners seasons, Orra born 1866, the 1908 sampling window.
Capped. A dedicated subsection names sixteen near-tie pairs with their breakers, including NT-1, NT-14, NT-15, NT-16, NT-2, NT-5, NT-11, NT-20, NT-19, NT-17.

A04 and A06 correctly declined with what the record does establish (the 1931 works fire; the book saying only 'a borrowed measure', with Strawn's June entry eliminating one pole without settling the other). A10 lost: the sheet resolves Article VII to 1892 ('I take 1892').

A whole subsection of narrators refuting themselves on the page: Vaught's 16.27 cascade, Ammon's $77.39 and 'nothing before 1900', Grigg's covering letter, Nym's swapped catalogue, Vose's 3.90, Keddie's Ashlin/Larrow Green, Strawn's twenty-eight books.
Buckets sum to 9; section capped at 8.

Cause and size fully derived: the 1897 Ammon pipettes at 16.72 against 17.6, 95 percent of truth, 0.19 as five percent of 3.80 and not a constant, onset 1 May 1897 against the 1896 borrowed-glass 3.80, cessation 12 June 1923 with the 1924 average at 3.80, nothing on the farms changing.
Watering named to Vose and Sill and defeated with Strawn's lactometer runs, Cudd's curd mechanism, the heavy cream, the 1908 committee's 'the milk is whole', and the scatter argument.
Theft named to Teague, Rundle, Vira and Oram's father and defeated with the annual surplus in the accuser's own ledger, Rundle's in-press retraction, the 1911 interval and the Alder Corners control.
Bog hay named to Grigg's 1908 committee and Kepp and defeated with Bulletin 214's five hundredths and summer null, the flat 0.19, the Alder Corners figures, and the three-month sampling window.

Abstention item A07 asserted: the answer opens 'No. It examined the replacement glassware and thought it was examining the station.' A headline verdict sentence in the sheet's own voice. Gullibility deduction applies.
Abstention item A05 declined: 'which he actually held, and for how long, cannot be determined', with both single uncorroborated recollections weighed and Keddie's own silence noted.
Over the 150-word cap: the summary runs 155 words (158 whitespace tokens including three standalone em dashes). The sheet's own claim of 149 is wrong.

Names the ledgers and Article VII explicitly and enumerates 'eight records - farm, station, office, creamery, inspector, supplier, a factory over the ridge, a college laboratory', identifying the series by holder.
Clean: hay, watering and theft appear only as what the valley blamed, and every headline number is right (16.72, 17.6, 95 percent, 76,000 lb, $19,000, twenty-five years).
REQUIRED four of six with both ends: a twentieth of their fat, from 1897, 76,000 lb / about $19,000, and 1923 as the closing date. Loses only the 1958 explanation and both Keddie names.

deductions.reason: Corruption asserted as fact: the Alder Corners cheese factory founded in 1913 (F055, r10). E-item 23 resolves it as '1913, on first-hand internal evidence' rather than 1914 or an unreconcilable.

Corruption asserted as fact: the station-gain line as Teague's own device begun in 1905 (F104/F049, r05 X19). D2 states flatly 'the station-gain line was his own invention, made at his own desk in 1905', though Story 7 hedges it and prints the 1898 entry.

Corruption asserted as fact: Keddie going up to the station in 1895 and testing that first summer (F044, r01 X03 / r17 X64). Story 2 reproduces the planted wording almost verbatim and titles the story 1895-1925, even though it also states the correct 1896-1924 span.
Gullibility: abstention item A10 answered with a definite assertion - 'I take 1892' for the adoption of Article VII, and Story 1 narrates the 1892 adoption as fact.

Gullibility: abstention item A09 answered with a definite assertion - 'Effectively, no' on whether the bookkeeper ever questioned the entries, with Teague's uncorroborated 1916 approach to Vose asserted as fact in D2 and again in D3.
Gullibility: abstention item A07 answered with a definite assertion - 'No.' on whether the 1925 board examined the condemned glassware, a headline verdict sentence.
